Changes in texture when lines or supporting layers enter and leave
supporting: Describing texture with comparative terms such as thin, dense, transparent, and thick

claims.claim: Texture concerns the ways musical lines interact; it can be described in relative density terms such as thin, thick, transparent, or dense.
Monophonic texture has a single melodic line, whether it is performed by one person or as a single line together.
In introductory descriptions, homophonic texture centers a melody with accompaniment, often chords or another supporting layer.
Polyphonic texture contains two or more independent melodic lines that matter to the musical activity.
Texture is not synonymous with loudness: dynamics concern volume, whereas texture concerns the arrangement and interaction of lines or layers.
The three basic labels are useful listening tools, but a responsible description first states what is audible and avoids forcing a single label onto a changing or culturally specific practice.
